content: When rendering issue badges in seeds, formatters must receive a closedBlockerIds set. Compute once per command: const closedBlockerIds = new Set(allIssues.filter(i => i.status === 'closed').map(i => i.id)). Pass to formatIssueOneLine, formatIssueOneLineCompact, printIssueOneLine. Without the set, issues whose blockers have all been closed still render with [blocked] tag. Call sites: src/commands/{list,ready,blocked,show,search,dep,tpl}.ts.

When porting the L5 governance baseline (.github/) into a sub-repo from templates/l5-toolkit/github/: issue templates use a <cli> placeholder that must be replaced with the repo's binary name (sd for seeds), and ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml's discussions URL must point at the per-repo GitHub (https://github.com/jayminwest/seeds/discussions), not the os-eco meta-repo. dependabot.yml and pull_request_template.md copy verbatim (already neutral). Do not touch pre-existing .github/workflows/.

name: l5-config-port-adapt-to-baseline
description: Porting L5 toolkit lint/dup/dep configs into a sub-repo with existing code: biome's noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity (cap 15) flags pre-existing command/parser functions — list offenders in a biome overrides[] block with the rule 'off' (mirrors canopy) so the cap governs new code without a refactor (commit guidance forbids source changes in scaffolding). jscpd threshold is adapted to current state: seeds baseline was 3.46%, so threshold=4 (not the ideal 3%) per porting-playbook 'adapt budgets/thresholds to current state'; ratchet-to-3% is a separate seed. knip: seeds tsconfig uses types:['bun-types'] (transitive via @types/bun) which knip reports as Unresolved — fix in knip.json with ignoreUnresolved:['bun-types'] rather than editing tsconfig (tsconfig edits are out of scope). extensions/**/*.ts entry+project globs match nothing today and emit non-fatal knip configuration hints; that is the intended future-proof tolerance, not an error. bunfig.toml: omit [test] root so bun's recursive discovery covers both src/ and extensions/.

name: l5-ratchet-port-colocated-budgets
description: Porting L5 toolkit ratchet scripts (check-file-sizes/check-debt-markers) into seeds with budgets co-located in scripts/ (not toolkit's ../budgets/ default): keep scripts verbatim (no logic change) and pass --budget scripts/<file>.json in the package.json check:size/check:debt entries. Adapt colocated *.test.ts: replace TOOLKIT_ROOT=resolve(import.meta.dir,'..') with SCRIPT_DIR=import.meta.dir, and point the CLI spawn + well-formed-budget reads at resolve(SCRIPT_DIR,'<file>'). The verbatim scripts trip biome noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity (scan() at 22/30 vs cap 15) so grandfather both into the existing biome.json complexity-off override rather than refactoring. Baseline file-size at threshold 500 with per-file budgets ceil(lines/50)*50+50 for the 5 files over 500; debt tracker prefixes sd-/seeds-/mx- as a hex regex plus #NNN and URL.

name: l5-coverage-reporters-port
description: Porting L5 coverage+reporters into seeds: ship toolkit check-coverage.ts verbatim (it has --budget/--repo-root flags) and point package.json at the co-located scripts/coverage-budgets.json via --budget, exactly like check:size/check:debt. Use canopy's report-test-timing.ts (default junit.xml at repo root, matching test:ci --reporter-outfile=junit.xml) rather than the toolkit default test-results/junit.xml. report-quality-metrics.ts needs its three budget reads repointed budgets/->scripts/ since seeds co-locates budgets. test:ci is self-contained (--coverage-reporter=text+lcov --coverage-dir=coverage --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=junit.xml), avoiding a bunfig [test] change. Budget shape is toolkit {functions,lines,packages} percentages in [0,100], floored down from observed (88.43/80.96 -> 87/80).

name: l5-agents-md-validator-port
description: Porting validate-agents-md.ts from l5-toolkit into seeds: the script trips seeds' biome noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity (max 15) on extractBacktickedPaths(23) and validate(19), same as the ratchet scripts — add scripts/validate-agents-md.ts to the biome.json overrides list that disables the rule (alongside check-file-sizes/check-debt-markers), don't refactor the verbatim toolkit source. AGENTS.md backticked paths are validated relative to repo root, so qualify bare module names (src/store.ts not store.ts); tokens with spaces/<>/= or trailing ... are skipped. check:agents only targets AGENTS.md by default, so RUNBOOK.md/SKILL.md paths aren't validated. Run lint:fix after copying the toolkit test (import-sort + format drift).

name: l5-pino-logger-and-governance-port
description: Porting L5 pino logging + governance into seeds: pino+pino-pretty go in devDependencies (seeds is a Bun-direct CLI, no bundle); src/log.ts exports createLog(options) + a default 'log' instance, resolving level INSIDE the factory (SEEDS_LOG_LEVEL > SEEDS_DEBUG===1 ? debug : info) so tests override via env+re-create. redact uses {paths,remove:true} with bare + '*.' one-level-nested keys (password/token/apiKey/secret/authorization) + headers.cookie/authorization, mirroring burrow. Seeds has NO ad-hoc debug output — all console.* is user-facing output.ts — so the only honest 'route through pino' point is index.ts's top-level catch, lazy-importing log and calling log.debug({err,cmd}) (silent at info, no happy-path logger cost). pino-pretty is referenced only as a transport string so add it to knip ignoreDependencies. pre-commit hook (toolkit version = lint+typecheck only, sub-2s) installed via prepare script: '[ -e .git ] && git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks || true'.

name: l5-milestone-seal-port
description: Final L5 seal for seeds (seeds-317e): wire check:all aggregator into package.json (check:size && check:debt && check:dups && check:deps && check:agents && check:coverage — NO check:bundle-size since seeds is unbundled) and extend .github/workflows/ci.yml in place (lint, typecheck, check:all, test:ci, report:test-timing/report:quality piped to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, upload junit.xml + coverage/lcov.info artifacts). seeds writes junit.xml to repo root (not test-results/ like the toolkit) — keep CI artifact paths in sync with the test:ci --reporter-outfile. junit.xml + coverage/ are gitignored; commit ONLY package.json + ci.yml. Do NOT run sd sync (mixes mission .seeds/ tracking into L5 history). All four gates exit 0 without loosening budgets: coverage funcs 88.45%/floor 87, lines 81.07%/floor 80.

sd doctor's gitattributes check/fix (src/commands/doctor.ts checkGitattributes + fixGitattributes) hardcoded only issues.jsonl + templates.jsonl merge=union lines, while sd init (init.ts MERGE_UNION_LINES) was updated to also write plans.jsonl. The two lists drifted, so doctor reported healthy and 'doctor --fix' never backfilled plans.jsonl — projects whose .gitattributes predated plans support got real git merge conflicts on plans.jsonl.
resolution: Exported MERGE_UNION_LINES from init.ts and made doctor's checkGitattributes + fixGitattributes loop over the shared constant for both detection and repair. Lesson: when one site writes a config list, the validator/repair site must consume the SAME constant, not a copy.

description: sync.test.ts git-failure flake: clearing GIT_AUTHOR_*/HOME to force a commit failure is unreliable. Bun drops empty-string env vars when inheriting process.env (so the in-process spawn never sees them cleared), and git still auto-derives an OS identity (username@hostname via gecos) unless invoked with '-c user.useConfigOnly=true' — env-injected (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT) or config-file useConfigOnly does NOT disable gecos, only the -c flag does.
resolution: Install a pre-commit hook that exits 1 in the broken test repo, pinned via repo-local 'git config core.hooksPath', so git commit fails deterministically regardless of host identity. Drop all GIT_* env manipulation from both git-failure tests.

description: check:debt flags the word TODO in user-facing strings (e.g. prime text) as an untracked debt marker
resolution: Reword the string rather than allowlisting it.

content: Do not run sd onboard / sd setup inside a git worktree to update repo files: findSeedsDir resolves to the main checkout. Use sd onboard --stdout and splice the output in.
